question: Has the collective discussed Diginex's path to profitability given the M&A spend?

beats.line: The collective hasn't discussed this lately; this draws on outside sources.
beats.action: A folded paper document drifts down onto a cream chip and settles flat.

beats.line: Diginex's profitability rests on a classic mergers and acquisitions maths problem.
beats.headline: INTEGRATION TAX
beats.action: The folded document unfolds into two paper ledger sheets; a torn-paper arrow slides between them and holds.

beats.line: The company is in active integration mode across four acquisitions.
beats.headline: 4 ACQUISITIONS
beats.action: The previous chip slides off the top edge as the arrow splits into four paper building blocks, taped side by side.

beats.line: Half-year admin costs climbed three point four million, reaching eight point one.
beats.headline: $8.1M G&A
beats.action: The previous chip flips away as the taped block row stacks upward into a rising paper bar; coins pile on its top and hold.

beats.line: Two point two million came from deal diligence and legal work.
beats.headline: 27% ONE-OFF
subjects: a shaded slice of the bar
beats.action: The previous chip is covered as a shaded slice tears out of the rising bar and lands beside a paper document.

beats.line: Resulticks, one point five billion, stretches integration into twenty twenty-seven.
beats.headline: $1.5B → 2027
beats.action: The previous chip slides off as the torn slice swells into a large paper block; a calendar strip unrolls from it across the frame.

beats.line: Leverage needs revenue up thirty to fifty percent, admin costs held flat.
beats.headline: +30–50% YOY
beats.action: The previous chip flips down as the calendar strip splits into two paper lines: one climbs steeply, the flat bar stays level beneath it.

beats.line: Without cross-sell, you get two siloed businesses and duplicate overhead.
beats.headline: CROSS-SELL OR TRAP
beats.action: The previous chip is covered as the climbing line bends into a broken paper bridge between two paper boxes that drift apart.

beats.line: Diginex has signalled focus on Brazil's seventy-seven billion dollar sustainability market.
beats.headline: $77B BRAZIL
beats.action: The previous chip slides off as the broken bridge folds into a paper map shape; a cutout ribbon unfurls over it and rests.

beats.line: Until the next reports land, profitability stays a narrative, not fact.
beats.headline: 2–3 REPORTS
beats.action: The previous chip flips away as the ribbon creases into three paper report cards; a paper hand enters and rests on the last one.
